stem: In a code, MANGO is written as OCPIQ. Using the same rule, what is the code for GRAPE?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Rule: each letter shifts forward by 2. M+2=O, A+2=C, N+2=P, G+2=I, O+2=Q. GRAPE: G+2=I, R+2=T, A+2=C, P+2=R, E+2=G. Code = ITCRG.
Student correctly applies +2 to the first four letters but miscounts the shift for E, writing H (E+3) instead of G (E+2).
Shifting every letter by 1 instead of 2 gives G to H, R to S, A to B, P to Q, E to F, which is HSBQF.
Shifting each letter by its position (1, 2, 3, 4, 5) gives H, T, D, T, J. The uniform rule was replaced with a progressive one.

explanation: From MANGO to OCPIQ, each letter moves forward by 2 positions in the alphabet: M(13)+2=O(15), A(1)+2=C(3), N(14)+2=P(16), G(7)+2=I(9), O(15)+2=Q(17). Applying the same +2 rule to GRAPE: G(7)+2=I(9), R(18)+2=T(20), A(1)+2=C(3), P(16)+2=R(18), E(5)+2=G(7). Code = ITCRG.

explanation_sections.punchline: Lock the rule by verifying at least two letters of the example: M+2=O and A+2=C both confirm a uniform +2 shift. That is the cracking move - a single-letter check could match a position-based rule; two letters rule it out.
explanation_sections.approach: Step 1 (derive rule from example): Check M(13)+2=O(15). Check A(1)+2=C(3). Both confirm uniform +2. Also verify N(14)+2=P(16) as a third check. Step 2 (apply to target): G(7)+2=I(9), R(18)+2=T(20), A(1)+2=C(3), P(16)+2=R(18), E(5)+2=G(7). Code = ITCRG. Step 3 (verify): read ITCRG back and confirm each letter is exactly 2 ahead of the corresponding GRAPE letter. This two-step recipe - verify rule on 2+ example pairs, then apply uniformly - works for any substitution-cipher coding question.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always verify the coding rule on at least two letters before applying it. A single match could fit both a uniform-shift rule and a position-indexed rule. Checking two letters eliminates the ambiguity.
explanation_sections.timing: About 80 seconds. Deriving the rule from MANGO: 25 seconds. Applying to GRAPE letter by letter: 40 seconds. Final check on the last letter: 15 seconds. The trap is option 2 (ITCRH) - it applies +2 correctly to the first four letters but slips to +3 on E. The last letter is the most error-prone.
